core_obligations: Derive the direct implication (base change of separated is separated) from the cited Morphisms of Spaces lemma (proof lines 1855-1858).
Unpack the hypothesis: each base change X_i \to Y_i separated means each \Delta_i : X_i \to X_i \times_{Y_i} X_i = Y_i \times_Y (X \times_Y X) is a closed immersion (proof lines 1860-1871).

Note the pulled-back fpqc covering of X \times_Y X and that each \Delta_i is the base change of \Delta, then conclude via lemma-descending-property-closed-immersion that \Delta is a closed immersion, i.e. f is separated (proof lines 1872-1880).
proof_roadmap: Handle the direct implication by base-change stability.
Reformulate separatedness of the base changes as closed immersiveness of their diagonals.
Descend the closed immersiveness of the diagonal along the fpqc covering.
difficulty_reason: The proof has two genuine halves: the direct implication from the cited base-change stability of separatedness; and the converse, which identifies each base-changed diagonal \Delta_i as a closed immersion, pulls the fpqc covering back to X \times_Y X, and descends the closed-immersion property of \Delta from the covering via the diagonal form of the fpqc descent lemma. The diagonal reformulation of separatedness driving the descent is the substance.
